name: Napoleon at Waterloo (SPI, Second Edition 1971)
blurb: 18 June 1815, 1 pm to 10 pm - Dunnigan's introductory division-scale Waterloo. Ten Game-Turns, forty Strength Points to break an army, seven French divisions to march off the north edge. Second Edition (1971) rules exactly as printed on the folio; the Third Edition is a separate game.

policy_ai.note: Seat model: each seat is Human, Basic AI (this transparent policy AI) or Champion AI (playbook/champion.json once a training run graduates); the Basic AI plays BOTH seats - Movement Phase attack planner (targets chosen by achievable odds, attackers massed on the adjacent hexes, artillery posted at two hexes with a clear line, the rest positioned by threat/terrain/cohesion/objective), Prussian entry, French exits (weak units from exit_turn, everyone once the Allies are demoralized), Combat Phase obligations resolved best-first with complete_assignment() as the always-legal fallback, and every pending (victor-chosen retreats, exchange payment, advances) - submits only through the gate; full 10-turn AI-vs-AI games complete and replay through verify_game. The 14-gene strategy family (strategy_naw.py) is the training substrate for the champion.

edition.printed: SPI Napoleon at Waterloo, Second Edition, copyright 1971 (folio: rules sheet, Examples of Attacks, counter set, map sheet with both CRT copies, TEC, Time Record, Demoralization Scale)
edition.not_this_game: The 1979 Third Edition is a different-sized battlefield (380 hexes vs 594), opposite hex-column parity, four reversed rules (E17/E21/E23/E28) - encoded as its own game, never as a flag here (Bruce 2026-08-13). Christian Holm Christensen's 2024 fan revamp (rules.pdf, CC BY-SA) is neither edition and is never cited.
edition.work_order: DECODE_PLAN.md; rule ids cited below are rows of ingest/rules_2nd_ed.json (127 verbatim rows with obligation + citation); charts in ingest/crt_2nd_ed.json and ingest/combat_charts.json; map graph ingest/hexgraph_2nd_ed.json; roster ingest/oob_2nd_ed.json

status: ENCODED (2026-08-18): all seven bites enforced by engine/naw.py; COVERAGE_MATRIX.md 109/111 ENFORCED + 1 UNREACHABLE + 1 OPEN (M.13 = platform UNDO policy NAW2-OR-3, Bruce). Validators: validate_data / movement / combat / battle / victory. Not on the menu until the seat-model refactor + Bruce's go.

grid.provenance: PREP-3 fit of Oliver's module map (Nap at Waterloo map 20mm hexes.jpg, 6623x5648): hex 0101 centre (833.95, 606.0), dx 205.55, dy 238.0, ODD columns half a hex LOWER (map_grid.json grid_px.oliver, even_down=false). Engine form: x0/y0 = that centre minus one dx/dy so col 1 row 1 = 0101; stagger_sign +1 + odd_row_carry 0 reproduces the neighbour formula PREP-5 PROVED (hexgraph_2nd_ed.json). validate_data.py asserts engine adjacency == the proved graph on all 594 hexes and maps every module at-start pixel (module_oob.json) to its printed hex, 44/44. The printed 2nd Ed map carries NO hex numbers; the CCRR scheme is ours (0101 = NW-most hex). NEVER share hex arithmetic with the 3rd Edition (opposite parity).

guide.victory: The French win by destroying forty Allied Combat Strength Points before losing forty of their own AND exiting seven French units off the north edge through the eleven arrowed hexes by the end of Game-Turn 10 (1 pm to 10 pm). The Allies win by destroying forty French Strength Points first. Forty Allied points lost without the seven exits = Allied DEMORALIZATION (all Allied attacks one odds column worse, all French attacks one better) and the best the Allies can then reach is a draw. Prussians (nine units, 34 points) enter anywhere on the east edge at the start of the Allied second turn.

sides.cite: PCS-05: French blue = First Player's army; British red and Prussian green = Second Player's army. SEQ-02: French Player-Turn first. detect_tokens = counter image basenames (the board layer's unit name), Allied listed FIRST because substring matching would otherwise read the French token NAW_1_1 inside the Allied NAW_1_10; scenario units carry explicit sides

stats.note: [att, def, ma] per counter image basename (board-layer unit name), longest fragment first so NAW_1_10 is tested before NAW_1_1; generated by build_data.py from ingest/oob_2nd_ed.json (Combat Strength serves attack and defence alike, PCS-02; Movement Allowance PCS-03). Scenario units carry explicit stats and the module piece name

unit_types.cite: PCS-04: three basic types - Infantry, Cavalry, Artillery divisions; type read off the printed counter photograph (PREP-4). Only artillery has a type-specific rule (ART-01..ART-18 bombardment at two hexes); infantry and cavalry differ only in their printed factors

hexside_rules.cite: MOV-16/MOV-17: the only Woods hexes any unit may enter are those traversed by Roads, and only by travelling along the road into and out of the Woods - every non-road hexside of a Woods/Road hex is closed in both directions (terrain.json sides.woods_edge)

zoc.cite: ZOC-01 every unit controls the six adjacent hexes; ZOC-02 at all times; MOV-10/ZOC-04 entering an enemy-controlled hex ends movement; MOV-11/ZOC-05 may not move through or out of one; MOV-13 a unit beginning its Movement Phase in an enemy ZOC may not move at all; ZOC-03 friendly ZOC never inhibits; ZOC-08 mutual

movement.note: Every enterable hex costs exactly one Movement Point (TEC rows 1-2, MOV-02/MOV-05); roads have no movement effect (TEC row 1); Woods entry prohibited (TEC row 3, MOV-18) - 99 MP here so no unit can afford it, the gate states the prohibition outright. MOV-07 through friendly units; MOV-08 never through or into enemy units; MOV-09 stacking PROHIBITED - no unit may finish its Movement Phase in the same hex as any other unit; MOV-06 consecutive hexes; MOV-20 no transfer or accumulation of MPs. All of this is DATA in bite 1; the naw gate class enforces it from bite 2.

classes.note: generated by build_data.py from the scenario roster: unit type from the printed counter photograph (PREP-4); 'prussian' = the nine Time Record arrivals (Allied for every rule, REI-05)

combat._status: ENFORCED (bites 3-5, engine/naw.py): arithmetic + per-attack legality (validate_combat.py: 27/27 printed Examples of Attacks, 60/60 CRT), the battle action with the fixed mandatory-attack assignment and forward check (validate_battle.py: 150 random positions, complete_assignment proof), result application AE/Ar/EX/Dr/DE with victor-chosen retreats, disruption chains, advances (attacker and defender), exchange payment and artillery immunity, and six full random games replayed by verify_game.

clamp.printed: Attacks executed at worse than “1 to 5” are treated as “1 to 5”; attacks executed at greater than “6 to 1” are treated as “6 to 1”.

crt.rounding: Attacker's total Combat Strength vs defender's total, expressed as a ratio and ROUNDED OFF IN FAVOUR OF THE DEFENDER

results.EX: Exchange - the defender is eliminated and the attacker suffers a loss AT LEAST EQUAL in Strength Points, made up only from units directly involved in that attack

crt.cite: folio p.5 Combat Resolution Table (printed twice, both copies agree cell for cell), read 4x - ingest/crt_2nd_ed.json; CBT-01/CBT-02 odds and rounding; validation corpus = the 27 printed Examples of Attacks (ingest/worked_examples.json, example_check.json 27/27)

terrain_effects.cite: TEC row 2 'Towns &  Woods/Roads - Defending unit DOUBLES its Combat Strength. Combat Strength remains at normal value when units attack from such terrain' + CBT-18 (Towns); ruling NAW2-D4 (Bruce 2026-08-14) follows the chart, independently corroborated by the printed 1979 sheet grouping Building + Woods-Road; printed examples EX-03/EX-04 prove an attacker in a Town gets nothing

procedure.adjacency: CBT-05 attackers must be adjacent (exception: artillery bombardment)
procedure.mandatory: CBT-06 ALL enemy units adjacent to friendly units MUST be attacked; CBT-07 ALL friendly units adjacent to enemy units MUST participate; CBT-10 no defender attacked more than once, no attacker attacks more than once; CBT-08/CBT-09 the attacker chooses order and pairing; CBT-11 several attackers may combine on one defender (all adjacent); CBT-12 one attacker may attack several adjacent defenders (strengths totalled); CBT-13 diversionary attacks at poor odds are legal; CBT-17 a unit's strength is never split
procedure.immediate: CBT-04 each result is applied immediately before the next attack is resolved
procedure.open: none - C.7 RULED (NAW2-OR-6 A, Bruce 2026-08-17: obligations fixed at Combat Phase start, resolved live, lapse on lost contact); OR-5 closed by proof (star partition of the fixed contact graph; the gate's forward check keeps every reachable position completable)
procedure.adjacency_reading: several-on-several (EX-14) legal only when every non-bombarding attacker is adjacent to every defender - satisfies CBT-11 and CBT-12 together
procedure.results: AE adjacent attackers eliminated (bombarding artillery immune); Ar adjacent attackers retreat one hex, direction chosen by the victorious DEFENDER (E21), bombarding artillery may voluntarily retreat (owner); EX defenders eliminated + attacker pays whole adjacent units >= PRINTED defender strength (attacker chooses; all adjacent when short; free when all bombarded); Dr defenders retreat one hex, attacker chooses; DE defenders eliminated. Retreat bars: enemy ZOC, off map, non-Road Woods, enemy hex; Woods/Road along the road; disruption of an uninvolved friend only when no empty safe hex, chain to completion or the retreater dies; advance optional, immediate, one hex, one unit per vacated hex, attackers after Dr/DE/EX (not bombarding), defenders after Ar/AE

artillery.cite: ART-01 artillery may bombard from two hexes; ART-06 never forced to bombard; ART-02/ART-07/ART-10 adjacent artillery MUST participate and suffers all results; ART-03/ART-04/ART-09 bombarding artillery is never destroyed or retreated by the result (ART-11 may voluntarily take an Ar); ART-05/ART-12 co-operating non-artillery units always suffer results; ART-13 bombardment targets a single unit; ART-14 adjacent artillery may attack all adjacent units; ART-15 no range on defence; ART-16 may fire over units and Town hexes; ART-17 may NOT fire over a Woods hex; ART-18 bombarding artillery may not advance
artillery.los_reading: SPI 1979 Terrain Key (publisher clarification of the identical 2nd Ed rule): Woods and Woods-Road hexes block bombardment over them; a bent two-hex shot is open if either candidate intervening hex is clear ('0803 could not fire into 0805 but could fire into 0705 and 0905 because of the intervening woods in 0804'); artillery may bombard INTO Woods-Road hexes. NAW2-OR-9 closed.

retreat.who_chooses: the VICTORIOUS player, for Ar and Dr alike (E21 - the 3rd Edition reverses this)
retreat.disruption: if the only safe hex holds an uninvolved friendly unit, that unit is displaced (moved back by the victorious player as if retreating) and the retreating unit takes its hex; the displaced unit may not be forced into enemy units, Zones of Control or woods; if that would be its only path the uninvolved unit is NOT disrupted and the retreating unit is eliminated instead; chains are legal; disrupted artillery may not fire in that Combat Phase
retreat.advance: optional, immediate, one hex into the vacated hex after Dr/DE/EX (never compulsory; legal even in enemy ZOC, CBT-15); advancing units may not participate in another attack or defence in that Combat Phase (X2); no MP cost (CBT-16); bombarding artillery may not advance (ART-18)
retreat.cite: folio p.5 RETREAT AND ADVANCE AS A RESULT OF COMBAT + DISRUPTION + OPTIONAL ADVANCE (British/Prussian half only - NAW2-SD-2), EXPLANATION OF RESULTS (both halves), ingest/combat_charts.json verbatim; CBT-14/CBT-15/CBT-16
retreat.open: NAW2-SD-3 - may a DISRUPTED unit be pushed into a Woods/Road hex (retreat bar says 'non-Road Woods', disruption bar says bare 'woods')? OPEN for Bruce

reinforcements.entry_hex_rule: any hex of column 27 (the East edge, 22 hexes; 4 are Woods and never enterable) that holds no enemy unit, lies in no enemy ZOC and holds no friendly unit; the entering unit pays 1 MP and may spend the rest of its Movement Allowance and fight this turn
reinforcements.delay: not permitted while any due unit has a legal entry hex (end_movement is refused); a unit with no legal entry hex enters at the first later Movement Phase it can, with the reason logged
reinforcements.cite: REI-01 (beginning of the Allied Player's second turn; Time Record 2 pm 'Prussians enter'), REI-02 (anywhere along the East edge, as many points as desired), REI-03 (placing expends one MP - printed 'extends', NAW2-SD-1), REI-04 (move and fight on entry), REI-05 (Prussian losses are Allied losses), REI-06 (may not be deliberately delayed - NAW2-OR-4 reading A), REI-07 (never leave the map); entry-hex bars = MOV-08 (enemy hex), MOV-16 (Woods), SPI 1979 7.2 (no entry into an enemy ZOC - publisher clarification), stacking MOV-09

exit.cite: VIC-08 French units exit only from the arrowed hexes (eleven, columns 01-11 of row 01, read off the printed map); VIC-09 exiting expends one Movement Point; VIC-10 exited units may not return; VIC-11 need not exit together nor from one hex, before and/or after the forty points; VIC-12 Allied units may NEVER exit; VIC-13 French units retreated off the map by combat count as destroyed, not exited; VIC-06 exited units are not French losses

victory.check: immediate (VIC-07) - whichever side reaches its condition first wins at once, mid Player-Turn included
victory.french_win: forty Allied Combat Strength Points destroyed BEFORE forty French, AND seven French units exited by the end of Game-Turn 10 (VIC-01/VIC-02)
victory.allied_win: forty French Combat Strength Points destroyed before forty Allied (VIC-03)
victory.draw: neither side reaches forty; or the French reach forty but fail the seven exits (VIC-04)
victory.simultaneous: both sides reach forty at the same instant (an EX): French win if seven already exited, otherwise the ALLIED player wins (VIC-14 - the folio's own case: 'If the French Player has NOT done so, then the Allied Player would be declared the winner')
victory.ledger: one printed Demoralization Scale, cells 1-40, shared: the engine keeps both running totals of printed Combat Strength destroyed (VIC-05); Prussian losses are Allied losses (REI-05); exited French units are not losses (VIC-06); first_forty records which side reached forty first (VIC-02) or 'both' (VIC-14)

demoralization.trigger: forty Allied Strength Points destroyed while fewer than seven French units have exited (DEM-01); immediate, mid Player-Turn included (DEM-02); permanent (DEM-03)
demoralization.consequence: the best the Allies can then reach is a draw (DEM-04, derived state - never a gate check); destroying forty French points afterwards is not an Allied win and relieves nothing (DEM-09); the French are never demoralized (DEM-05)
demoralization.end_of_table: a shifted column past 1:5 or 6:1 stays at the printed end column (clamp) - NAW2-OR-19 reading A; SPI 1979 6.2 'ratios beyond the table's ends are treated as the end column'

source_defects.note: Defects in the ORIGINAL PUBLISHED GAME (SPI 1971 folio) found during decode-prep and encoding - spec #21. Authority ladder (as amended 2026-08-09): official errata > publisher/tournament clarification or the game/module creator's answer > proven outcome-equivalence. SPI no longer exists and no errata for the 1971 folio has been found: for this game the only remaining rung is a declared ruling by Bruce (DECODE_PLAN.md section 4 - direction call surfaced). An OPEN entry blocks the cells it touches; the gate is not written past it.

list.defect: The rules sheet says 'Units defending in Towns DOUBLE their strength (on defense)' and never mentions Woods/Roads; the Terrain Effects Chart on the same folio prints 'Towns &  Woods/Roads' as ONE row with one shared effect cell 'Defending unit DOUBLES its Combat Strength'. Both are primary components of the same edition; the 27 printed examples never place a defender in a Woods/Road hex.
list.resolution: FOLLOW THE CHART: a defender in a Town OR a Woods/Road hex doubles; attacking from either confers nothing. Blast radius five hexes (the woods_road class).
list.authority: DECLARED RULING - Bruce, 2026-08-14 (judgement between printed equals). Independently corroborated the same evening by the printed 1979 sheet, whose key groups Building + Woods-Road with 'Defender in hex is doubled'.

list.defect: Folio p.1 case (B.) prints 'The act of placing a Prussian unit on the map extends one Movement Point', where the same page prints the mirror-image action correctly two columns later: 'The Act of exiting from the edge of the map expends one Movement Point.'
list.resolution: Enforced as 'expends': placing a Prussian unit on the map costs one Movement Point.
list.authority: PROVEN OUTCOME-EQUIVALENCE (same document, correct construction for the mirror case; no reading of 'extends' yields a coherent alternative rule).

list.defect: The two player-aid halves of the printed map sheet are not mirrors: the French half carries the Terrain Effects Chart and no retreat rules; the British/Prussian half carries RETREAT AND ADVANCE, DISRUPTION and the optional advance and no Terrain Effects Chart. Only the Explanation of Results and the CRT grid are printed twice. The rules sheet contains no retreat procedure at all.
list.resolution: No rules effect - the engine enforces every printed rule regardless of which half prints it. Registered because a human player consulting one half sincerely believes rules do not exist.
list.authority: OBSERVED - two independent readings of the printed sheet (PREP-5).

list.defect: The retreat bar forbids retreating 'into non-Road Woods'; the DISRUPTION paragraph two paragraphs later forbids forcing the displaced unit 'into Enemy units or Zones of Control or woods' - bare 'woods', and it also omits the retreat bar's 'off the map'. Whether a disrupted unit may be pushed into one of the five Woods/Road hexes is undefined; NAW2-D4 makes those hexes defensively valuable, sharpening the question.
list.resolution: RESOLVED (reading A): a displaced unit is barred exactly where a retreating unit is barred - enemy units, enemy ZOC, off the map, non-Road Woods; a Woods/Road hex is allowed across its road hexside. Lands in bite 5.
list.authority: PUBLISHER CLARIFICATION - SPI's 1979 3rd Edition [6.4] (safe hex = a traversable hex not in an enemy ZOC), [4.2] (Woods entered/left only via road hexsides 'even when advancing or retreating due to combat'), [6.5] (displaced units retreat to safe hexes). Same designer, same publisher, same rule rewritten.

list.defect: Results apply immediately (CBT-04) and attacks resolve one at a time, so the set of 'adjacent enemy units' changes during the Combat Phase; the sheet does not say whether the mandatory-attack obligations (every adjacent enemy attacked, every adjacent friendly participating, nobody twice) are fixed at phase start or re-evaluated after each result - two defensible readings with different legal move sets. It also gives no relief clause for a position where no complete assignment exists.
list.resolution: RULED: obligations (every adjacent enemy attacked, every adjacent friendly attacks, nobody twice) are FIXED at the start of the Combat Phase; each attack resolves on the live board; an obligation lapses when its contact no longer exists (the enemy retreated/was eliminated, or the friendly advanced - an advanced unit leaves the list). With the list fixed a complete assignment always exists (a unit may attack every enemy it touches, so any uncovered enemy folds into a neighbour's attack) - to be PROVED by validator, closing NAW2-OR-5 without a ruling.
list.authority: DECLARED RULING - Bruce, 2026-08-17 (table practice; the printed Examples of Attacks show one board with two complete partitions; the only referee-enforceable reading). SPI 1979 [5.1]/[6.1] repeat the same words and do not decide it. Christian Holm Christensen asked the same evening; may overturn.
